Keep the existing structure so the setting is read as a region setting.", "uses": ["R1"], "after": []}, {"id": "P2", "file": "allocation/rations.py", "change": "Add winter_kits(household: Household, today=None) -> int. Look up the household's region settings via config.settings.region(household.region) (Household.region is the region code, R4). If the region dict has no winter_kit setting, return 0 — decide by the setting, not by climate. If it has the setting, count the household's people by reusing the existing ration_size(household, today) function (same household-size rules as food kits, with day = today or _today()), take people_per_kit from the winter_kit setting, and return max(1, math.floor(people / people_per_kit)) so every household in such a region gets at least one winter kit.", "uses": ["R2", "R3", "R4"], "after": ["P1"]}, {"id": "P3", "file": "inventory/stock.py", "change": "Add reserve_winter_kits(warehouse_id: str, qty: int, household_id: str) -> Reservation | None. If qty == 0, return None without calling reserve_stock (reserve_stock raises ValueError for qty <= 0). Otherwise return reserve_stock(warehouse_id, 'WINTER-KIT', qty, 72, household_id=household_id), reusing the existing reservation function with a 72-hour hold, and return its Reservation (including a pending reservation when stock is insufficient).", "uses": ["R5", "R6", "R7"], "after": []}]}}
